title: 'Barrage of bullets': Two South Simcoe Police officers have died in a line-of-duty shooting in Innisfil
subtitle: The Special Investigations Unit had invoked its mandate following a serious incident
article: Two South Simcoe Police Service officers died in a line-of-duty shooting on Tuesday evening (Oct. 11).

A media conference will be held at 1 p.m. today (Oct. 12) at Innisfil Town Hall. South Simcoe Police Service Chief John Van Dyke will read a prepared statement but will not be taking questions at this time.
More information has been released by the Special Investigations Unit (SIU), which has taken over the investigation.
At approximately 7:55 p.m., police responded to a disturbance at a Somers Boulevard home in the area of 25th Sideroad and 9th Line in Innisfil.
"There was an exchange of gunfire between the man and officers," SIU communications person Kristy Denette said in a press release.
Two officers were shot inside the home. The suspect, a 22-year-old man, was later pronounced dead at the scene following the interaction with police.
The wounded officers were rushed to a local hospital by emergency run, where one of them died. The second officer was airlifted to a Toronto trauma centre and has since succumbed to the injuries.
Both officers are now at the Ontario Coroner's office, where autopsies are anticipated.
At 10:50 p.m. on Tuesday night, South Simcoe police spokesperson Sue Sgambati said the Special Investigations Unit had invoked its mandate following a serious incident.
"As a result, the South Simcoe Police Service is unable to comment," Sgambati said in the press release.
The SIU investigates incidents involving officials where there is a serious injury, death, allegation of sexual assault or discharge of a firearm by an official at a person.

The SIU is urging anyone who may have information about this investigation, including video or photos, to contact the lead investigator at 1-800-787-8529 or online at: https://siu.on.ca/en/appeals.php.
York Regional Police are conducting an investigation into the details surrounding the shooting of the officers.

"(There's an) ongoing incident in South Simcoe tonight," retired police chief Andrew Fletcher shared on Twitter shortly after 10:20 p.m. on Tuesday evening. "Please await a formal statement from our Corporate Communications Officer and Acting Chief Van Dyke, and in the interim please pray for all those involved."
Multiple police sources - who weren't authorized to speak on the record about the incident - told Simcoe.com South Simcoe police were responding to a domestic call.
A suspect allegedly had a gun, and shots were fired, with one officer being struck in the head, a second in the arm.

On Tuesday night, a Simcoe.com reporter on scene counted 10 to 12 police vehicles on Somers Boulevard in Alcona in connection to the case. There was also a forensic identification unit and a paramedic vehicle.

One neighbour, who asked to be identified only as Kevin due to the seriousness of the incident, lives about 200 feet from the home where the occurrence happened. He's attended a garage sale there once, but doesn't know those neighbours well.
Kevin went into his backyard to take something off his barbecue around 9:15 p.m., when he heard a "barrage of bullets" - somewhere between seven and 12 in all.

"They were in such quick succession," he said. "It was 'pop, pop, pop, pop, pop' - very quick. It sounded like it was coming from one firearm, not three. It sounded like someone was emptying a clip. It was all the same sound."
He ran inside his house.

"I ran in to see my wife and I said 'did you hear those bullets?' She said 'no'," he said. "As soon as I said that, my neighbour across the street called. They live two doors down from where the incident happened. She said there's something crazy going on."
Kevin went outside and saw several police vehicles pull up and stop in front of him. The officers got out of their vehicles and entered the suspect's residence.
"They clearly sounded extremely distraught," Kevin said.
Officers began yelling for a towel, then asked him to begin moving cruisers so ambulances could get through to the scene.

"I have young children and a loving family," Kevin said. "Gunshots go off in our neighbourhood, a peaceful neighbourhood, it's extremely scary. I may have light shock, being so close to danger. Right now, I'm mostly concerned about the safety of the police officers. These guys work really hard for us."
Kevin says he saw two people transported to hospital - at least one was an officer.
John Ridge has lived on Somers for more than a quarter of a century. His home is about 10 doors north of the scene.
"This is the worst thing I've seen here so far," he said.
Somers is a blend of older lots with mature trees and newer houses, Ridge said.
He saw two police vehicle speed by around 8:30 p.m., but went to bed shortly afterward and didn't hear "a damn thing" after that.
"I woke up this morning and said 'what the hell happened?'" Ridge said.

He said he met an older adult who was living in the house just a few weeks ago, and described him as "a real nice guy," though he couldn't confirm to Simcoe.com whether other people were living in the house at the time.
Barrie police spokesperson Peter Leon said officers are assisting South Simcoe in the investigation.

Premier Doug Ford tweeted Wednesday morning: "I'm heartbroken to learn that two @SouthSimcoePS officers were killed in the line of duty. We are praying for the officers' families and all the police officers who put their lives on the line to protect our communities."
Condolences also came in from Barrie police and the city's mayor Jeff Lehman and fire chief Cory Mainprize.

"Our hearts are heavy today as we mourn two South Simcoe police officers killed in the line of duty last night," Barrie police said in a Twitter post. "Our thoughts are with the officers' families, friends and colleagues on this tragic day."
Lehman said he was "devastated for our close friends and neighbours ... and for a community in shock and mourning today."
"As your next door neighbours, we're here to support both the police service and the community of Innisfil however we can," he said.
Mainprize expressed similar sentiment.

"Our @Barrie_Fire team is heartbroken to hear of the line of duty death and critical injury of the @SouthSimcoePS members," he said. "Our thoughts and prayers to all the families, officers, friends, and the entire Innisfil community."

The Police Association of Ontario released a statement, too, noting its members are "in mourning after the devastating events" and suggesting these incidents "affect our tight-knit community on a deep level."

"I offer sincere condolences to the families, friends and colleagues of the officers we lost last night; our policing community grieves with them together," association president Mark Baxter said. "This is a tremendous loss for our entire policing community and incidents like this cause us all to pause and reflect. This provides a stark reminder of the dangers our members put themselves in every day to protect the communities they serve. This is a reminder of the unwavering courage, bravery and devotion they display every time they put on their uniform."
Four officers have died in Ontario over the last month, he said.
The officers were "leaders in helping with mental health and distress calls," Barrie-Innisfil MPP Andrea Khanjin said.

"It's a heartbreaking and devastating time," she said. "Words cannot express my deep and profound sadness. The days ahead will be difficult for everyone impacted by this tragedy, and our community as a whole. The horrible news reminds us of the dangers that our brave men and women in public service face every day, the bravery it takes to choose to serve for the greater good as a police officer, and the sacrifices they take on to keep our communities safe."
